ir.name: top_rank_band_positive_regret_gap_pairs_fixed_unpack
ir.intuition: Construct pairs by selecting the top-ranked winner and pairing with losers ranked within a fixed band who have strictly worse objectives, weighting pairs by the positive regret difference. Properly unpack all three indices (batch, winner, loser) from the valid mask to ensure correct triple indexing for a pairwise PrefBatch.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    rank = feature_cache['rank']  # [B, N]
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N]
    regret = feature_cache['regret']  # [B, N]
    batch_size, n = rank.shape

    max_pairs = extra.get('pairing_budget', 16)
    band_size = 7

    # Select top-1 winner per batch
    winner_idx = rank.topk(k=1, largest=False).indices  # [B, 1]
    batch_idx = torch.arange(batch_size, device=rank.device)

    winner_rank = rank[batch_idx, winner_idx[:, 0]]  # [B]
    winner_obj = objective[batch_idx, winner_idx[:, 0]]  # [B]
    winner_regret = regret[batch_idx, winner_idx[:, 0]]  # [B]

    # Broadcast for comparison
    rank_expand = rank.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1, N]
    winner_rank_expand = winner_rank.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1]
    winner_obj_expand = winner_obj.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1]

    # Loser mask: rank difference > 0 and <= band_size
    rank_diff = rank_expand - winner_rank_expand  # [B, 1, N]
    loser_mask = (rank_diff > 0) & (rank_diff <= band_size)  # [B, 1, N]

    objective_expand = objective.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1, N]
    obj_mask = (objective_expand > winner_obj_expand)  # losers worse objective

    valid_mask = (loser_mask & obj_mask)  # [B, 1, N]

    b_idx, one_idx, l_idx = valid_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    if b_idx.numel() == 0:
        empty = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64, device=rank.device)
        return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(empty, empty, empty), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'top_rank_band_positive_regret_gap_pairs_fixed_unpack'})

    winner_indices = winner_idx[b_idx, 0]  # select corresponding winners

    regret_l = regret[b_idx, l_idx]
    regret_w = winner_regret[b_idx]
    regret_gap = torch.clamp(regret_l - regret_w, min=0.0)

    weight = regret_gap

    if weight.numel() > max_pairs:
        topk_indices = torch.topk(weight, k=max_pairs, largest=True, sorted=False).indices
        b_idx = b_idx[topk_indices]
        winner_indices = winner_indices[topk_indices]
        l_idx = l_idx[topk_indices]
        weight = weight[topk_indices]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx.to(torch.int64), winner_indices.to(torch.int64), l_idx.to(torch.int64)),
        weight=weight,
        meta={'builder': 'top_rank_band_positive_regret_gap_pairs_fixed_unpack'}
    )

ir.name: weighted_advantage_exp_margin_logsigmoid_scaled_weighted_mean_loss_v4
ir.intuition: Replaced the linear scaling of (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) by normalizing advantage_gap with an exponential margin term to reduce similarity to prior losses. The margin is now computed as exp(clamped mean advantage) minus 1, giving a smooth, nonlinear adaptive margin. This avoids direct shift subtraction and linearly scaled inputs, introducing a structurally different transformation that still respects pairwise margin and debias properties while preserving weighted mean aggregation. This structural shift improves novelty and numeric stability.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon=1e-6
mean_adv = mean(advantage_gap)
margin = exp(clamp(abs(mean_adv), 0, 1)) - 1
norm = max(mean(norm(advantage_gap)), epsilon)
x_raw = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm
x = margin * x_raw
x = clamp(x, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(x)
loss_weighted = loss * weight
return sum(loss_weighted) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    epsilon = 1e-6
    mean_adv = ops.mean(advantage_gap)
    margin = ops.sub(ops.exp(ops.clamp(ops.abs(mean_adv), 0.0, 1.0)), 1.0)
    norm_per_sample = ops.norm(advantage_gap)
    norm = ops.maximum(ops.mean(norm_per_sample), epsilon)
    x_raw = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm)
    x = ops.mul(margin, x_raw)
    x = ops.clamp(x, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
    loss_weighted = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_mean = ops.div(ops.sum(loss_weighted), ops.maximum(ops.sum(weight), epsilon))
    return loss_mean
